chunks: The Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-Khaṭṭāb and al-Ḥasan ibn Mūsā al-Khashshāb, from Yazīd ibn Isḥāq, from Hārūn ibn Ḥamzah al-Ghanawī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
For ghusl and istinjāʾ, what suffices you is that with which you have wetted your hand.

key_terms.الِاسْتِنْجَاءِ: istinjāʾ; cleansing the private parts after relieving oneself
key_terms.الْغُسْلِ: ghusl; the ritual bath required for major ritual impurity
key_terms.بَلَلْتَ: you wetted; refers to moistening with water
key_terms.يَدَكَ: your hand; the measure mentioned for sufficiency in this report
key_terms.يُجْزِيكَ: it suffices you; indicates legal adequacy

ai.seo_question: How much water is sufficient for ghusl and istinjāʾ according to a hadith from Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a concise legal ruling related to ritual purification in the context of janābah. It indicates that a small amount of water, enough to wet the hand, suffices for ghusl and istinjāʾ in this specific wording.
